extracted.intended_audience: UKRI executives, Board members, DSIT (sponsor department) officials, and governance/legal teams
extracted.subtask_description: Framework of governance, responsibilities and reporting for UKRI’s Chief Executive (as Accounting Officer), Board, Chair, Councils, Committees and sponsor department interactions. Sets standards for composition, duties, escalation, delegation, assurance, appointments and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation of internal disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Within UKRI, the issue should be escalated within the organisation at working level, then to the relevant Director and/or working level committee Chair, and ultimately to the CEO as Accounting Officer and/or the UKRI Chair (as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the dispute is resolved, both parties should endeavour to learn the lessons from this process, and guidance should be recorded and communicated within each organisation to aid future deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information and data request consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for information is received under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, or the Data Protection Act 1998 or 2018, the party receiving the request will consult with the other party prior to any disclosure of information that may affect the other party’s responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reporting of legal risk and litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall provide a quarterly update to the sponsor on the existence of any active litigation and any threatened or reasonably anticipated litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties acknowledge importance of timely communication of legal risks to the sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation protocol and handling privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each substantial piece of litigation involving UKRI, the parties will agree a litigation protocol including provisions to ensure appropriate and timely reporting and protection of legally privileged information transmitted to the sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until a protocol is agreed, ensure material developments are communicated timely; legally privileged documents are clearly marked; individuals handling privileged documents know principles to protect privilege; circulation of privileged information within government occurs only as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting Officer personal responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Executive as Accounting Officer (AO) is personally responsible for safeguarding the public funds for which they have charge; for ensuring propriety, regularity, value for money and feasibility in the handling of those public funds; and for the day-to-day operations and management of UKRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should ensure UKRI is run on the basis of the standards set out in Box 3.1 of Managing Public Money (MPM) and comply with responsibilities set in the AO appointment letter issued by the PAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO strategic and representational duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO’s general responsibilities include: developing dialogue and partnerships with research, business and other user communities; developing proposals for the UKRI Strategy and leading implementation; promoting recruitment, retention and development of staff; and representing UKRI to the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting to Parliament and public duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities include signing the accounts and ensuring proper records; preparing and signing a Governance Statement; ensuring effective procedures for handling complaints in accordance with Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman’s Principles; and acting in accordance with MPM and other departmental guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure familiarity with governing legislation, this framework, delegation and settlement letters, maintain internal monitoring mechanisms for non-compliance, and give evidence (normally with the PAO) when summoned before the Public Accounts Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities to sponsor department (DSIT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO must establish, in agreement with DSIT, UKRI’s corporate and business plans aligned with DSIT’s wider strategic aims; inform DSIT of progress on policy objectives; provide timely forecasts and monitoring of performance and finance; notify DSIT promptly of likely over/under spends and take corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adherence to ministerial budget allocations; notify DSIT of significant problems whether detected by internal audit or otherwise; ensure Council Executive Chairs receive annual appraisals; maintain delegated authorities and personnel management policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely information to Board and DSIT
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO will ensure information necessary for effective monitoring of performance is supplied both to the UKRI Board and to DSIT in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See referenced sections 43 and 44 for further details (not in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: System of controls and assurance (AO duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO will establish a system of controls and assurance that ensure his/her Accounting Officer responsibilities are fulfilled and be able to demonstrate to the PAO that UKRI has an effective assurance framework which facilitates clear accountability and efficient decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO responsibilities to the Principal Accounting Officer (PAO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO will ensure the DSIT Permanent Secretary as PAO is assured on the discharge of delegated AO responsibilities, including by providing an Accounting Officer assessment ahead of major or potentially contentious investments, ensuring DSIT officials are aware of emerging material risks, being open about internal processes and escalating problems appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure guidance from the PAO is disseminated within UKRI and maintain clear lines of communication between UKRI staff and DSIT officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advising the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Executive is responsible for advising the Board on the discharge of their responsibilities, on UKRI’s performance compared with its aims and objectives, and ensuring financial considerations are taken fully into account by the Board at all stages in reaching and executing its decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure financial appraisal techniques are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing conflicts between CEO and Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Executive should follow the advice and direction of the Board, except in very exceptional circumstances with a clear cut and transparent rationale for not doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CEO (AO) considers a Board course of action would infringe propriety, regularity, prudence, feasibility or ethics, they should reject it, allow full Board discussion, bring conflicts to the PAO and Secretary of State, and (if agreed with Secretary of State) write a letter of justification to the Chair and copy the Treasury Officer of Accounts. The Secretary of State may direct per MPM if they agree with the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition and corporate governance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will have a Board in line with good standards of corporate governance and its establishing statute; the role of the Board is to run UKRI and deliver objectives in accordance with statutory, regulatory and common law duties and responsibilities under this framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed responsibilities set out in Board terms of reference; remuneration disclosed in line with Government Financial Reporting Manual (FReM). Board to consist of Chair, CEO, CFO and 9-12 independent non-executives with a balance of skills; majority independent non-executive members to ensure constructive challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board committees minimum requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may set up such committees as it deems necessary. As a minimum, UKRI should establish an Audit and Risk Assurance Committee and a Nominations and Remuneration Committee chaired by an independent and appropriately qualified non-executive member of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board retains responsibility for and endorses final decisions in areas committees assist; Chair should ensure sufficient time is allowed at Board for committees to report; terms of reference should set responsibilities and delegated authority; ensure membership refreshed periodically and non-execs not over-burdened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and Risk Assurance Committee (ARAC) remit
rubrics_metrics.description: ARAC is an advisory committee that supports the UKRI Board and Accounting Officer by reviewing the comprehensiveness and reliability of assurances on governance, risk management, the control environment, performance information, financial reporting and the integrity of the annual report and accounts, and gaining assurance that there is an adequate and effective risk management and assurance framework in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide oversight and independent challenge regarding policy and process implementation; review UKRI’s overall operational performance and integrity of financial statements; roles, responsibilities and membership set out in published terms of reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations and Remuneration Committee (NomCo) remit
rubrics_metrics.description: NomCo is an advisory committee which supports the Board in determining the composition and effectiveness of the Councils, will agree appointment of Council members, and advises on appropriate remuneration for Ministerial appointments and senior officials earning £100,000 or above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT will require assurance that remuneration proposals comply with latest public sector pay policy and guidance applicable to NDPBs; DSIT will inform UKRI of relevant public sector pay policy in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board duties: strategic leadership and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is specifically responsible for establishing and taking forward the strategic aims and objectives of UKRI consistent with overall strategic direction and policy/resources framework; providing effective leadership within a framework of prudent and effective controls enabling risk assessment and management; ensuring resources are in place to meet objectives; reviewing management performance; and ensuring receipt and review of regular financial and management information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure Board is kept informed of changes likely to impact strategic direction or targets and determine steps needed, including bringing matters to Minister and PAO attention where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and familiarity with governance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board must ensure statutory or administrative requirements for use of public funds are complied with, operate within limits of statutory authority and any delegated authority agreed with sponsor department, and in reaching decisions take into account guidance issued by the sponsor department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board members should be familiar with this framework document, any delegation or settlement letters, and have mechanisms for monitoring, governance and external reporting regarding conditions arising from those documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance over risk management and internal control
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board should ensure effective arrangements are in place to provide assurance on risk management, governance and internal control and should make a strategic choice about the style, shape and quality of risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead assessment and management of opportunity and risk; ensure effective arrangements to provide assurance over design and operation of risk management, governance and internal control in line with the Orange Book; must set up an Audit and Risk Assurance Committee chaired by an independent qualified non-exec and assure itself of adequacy and effectiveness of risk framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board role in strategy development and ministerial advice
rubrics_metrics.description: As set out in the HER Act, and if asked by the Secretary of State, the Board will be responsible for development of the UKRI Strategy and present it to the Secretary of State for approval; the Board will ensure Secretary is kept informed of changes likely to impact strategic direction or attainability of targets; and advise the Secretary of State on strategic priorities and balance of funding between research disciplines and dual support funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of State’s powers and obligations regarding the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State may ask the Board to oversee development of UKRI Strategy; must consider any advice from the Board regarding funding allocation; may provide grants and terms and conditions; has a power of direction regarding allocation/expenditure of grants; and may provide guidance short of a direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of State will have regard to the Haldane principle, the balanced funding principle and any Board advice when making funding allocations; has obligation to ensure Board has balance of skills via ministerial appointments in line with Government Code of Good Practice for Corporate Governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair’s leadership and governance responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair is responsible for leading the Board in delivery of its responsibilities, exercising duties in light of contract/appointment letter, Chair’s priorities from Secretary of State, statute and framework document; communications between Board and Secretary of State normally through the Chair; the Chair is bound by the Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies and Nolan Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair must ensure probity, policies and actions support Secretary of State’s wider strategic policies, work closely with DSIT Director General, meet Secretary of State (with CEO) at least annually, and meet regularly with Director General to brief on UKRI matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair’s specific leadership duties and board effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair has leadership responsibilities: formulating the Board’s strategy; ensuring Board takes proper account of Department guidance; promoting efficient and effective delivery; delivering high standards of regularity and propriety; and representing the Board’s views to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation that Board work and members are reviewed and working effectively, including annual evaluations and deeper assessments for re-appointment; seek stakeholder views in assessments; ensure balance of skills on Board; ensure continuous skills/training (financial management, risk management, public sector board membership); ensure Board Operating Framework and code of practice for members are in place; ensure members receive appraisals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Board members’ conduct and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Board members’ responsibilities specific to UKRI are set out in terms and conditions of public appointment. Individual board members should comply at all times with the Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies (including Nolan Principles), demonstrate adherence to 12 Principles of Governance for NEDs, not misuse information, comply with rules on gifts and hospitality, act in good faith and in the best interests of UKRI, and be familiar with applicable guidance from Cabinet Office, HM Treasury or wider government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Independent Member (SIM) role for UKRI Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State may designate one Non-Executive Board member to act as the UKRI Senior Independent Member (UKRI SIM). This role will primarily support the Chair and help to support the role of non-executives in UKRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIM helps provide assurance on effective operation of the Board and offers an independent route of escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI internal governance structure
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI is comprised of a Board, 9 Councils overseen by the Board, and a strategic and corporate centre coordinated by the Executive Committee led by the CEO. The Executive Committee provides strategy advice and is the day-to-day coordinating body; its membership includes the 9 Executive Chairs, CEO and CFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board supported at minimum by Audit, Risk, Assurance Committee and Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and responsibilities of Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI Councils (7 science and humanities councils, Innovate UK and Research England) are responsible for advising the Board and making decisions on scientific, research and innovation matters in their discipline-specific area as set out in the HER Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Councils deliver against discipline focus and interact with Board and Executive arrangements described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council composition and membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Council will consist of 5-12 independent (ordinary) members and an Executive Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Chairs are senior UKRI staff, managed by the UKRI CEO, delegated financial authority to make commitments on behalf of their Council and may be delegated additional responsibilities by the CEO per the Delegations Framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Chairs’ responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Chairs’ responsibilities include leadership of their field, prioritisation of budgets, development of delivery plans, ensuring future supply of skilled researchers and specialists essential to sustainability of UK’s research and innovation capacity, and engaging with their community to develop ideas and disseminate strategic outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Chairs undertake cross-cutting activity on behalf of UKRI and report to the CEO; they are delegated authority for managing budgets by the CEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary Council members’ responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary members should support and challenge the Executive Chair to ensure effective delivery of the Council’s mission by providing guidance, advice and recommendations on research, knowledge exchange, training and innovation; contributing to the development and implementation of the UKRI Strategy; providing independent scrutiny on performance, quality of portfolio and reporting of outputs/outcomes/impacts; advising on prioritisation of funding within the Council’s field; and encouraging collaborative working across Councils and the wider community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation principle from Board to Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will delegate responsibility for decision making to each Council in relation to their discipline area, adopting a principle of subsidiarity so that functions are delegated to Councils wherever it is effective to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HER Act requires the Board to consider overall effectiveness, efficiency and economy of UKRI when delegating functions; delegation methods include commissioning/approval of strategic delivery plans, budget allocation letters and delegation letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research England delegated responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Research England shall be delegated by the Board responsibilities including decision-making in respect of its delegated budget; operating on behalf of UKRI on institutionally-focused policy and funding issues regarding research and knowledge exchange in English higher education providers; working with devolved funding bodies to allocate funds across the UK when required; and evaluating its own policy and funding programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research England should engage with devolved administrations and devolved funding bodies to gather a UK-wide view of higher education sector-related policy issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee membership and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee, established by the HER Act, provides strategy advice to the UKRI Board and is the day-to-day coordinating body for executive activity; membership as a minimum consists of the 9 Executive Chairs, the UKRI CEO and the UKRI CFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It provides leadership across collective activities of separate Councils to ensure collaboration on strategy and operational matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Independent Member role for Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: One ordinary member of each Council will be appointed as Senior Independent Member to support the Executive Chair in chairing Council meetings, holding the council’s executive to account, assuring the UKRI Chair and Board of effective operation of the Council, and providing a route to escalate problems and concerns independently to the UKRI Chair and Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and evaluation of Board, Councils and Committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board, Councils, Executive Committee and their immediate sub-committees should be evaluated internally on an annual basis, with independent input at least once every 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should be in line with DSIT or public sector guidance (eg Corporate Governance in Central Government Departments Code and Guidance Note), include the Board, committees and individual members, be incorporated in line management appraisals of executive Board members and other appraisal processes, be coordinated by the relevant secretariat in consultation with the Chair (and SIM for Councils), and outcomes should inform the annual governance statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and Ministerial appointments governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulated public appointments to UKRI must adhere to the Governance Code and are subject to periodic audit by the Office of the Commissioner for Public Appointments; DSIT is accountable for making ministerial appointments to UKRI and will manage the process in accordance with Governance Code and HER Act provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT welcomes a minimum of 12 months’ notice for re-appointment recommendations, will advise the Secretary of State on appointments, manage recruitment panels, advise on role specifications, remuneration and composition, work with UKRI in a timely manner, and provide advice on remuneration regulations; UKRI will provide advice/recommendations to DSIT on remuneration for ministerial appointees and expense arrangements aligned with Managing Public Money requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and terms of Board and Council members
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State will appoint the UKRI Chair, CEO, CFO and 9–12 other independent Board members; the CEO, CFO and independent members are appointed by the Secretary of State in consultation with the UKRI Chair; one independent Board member will chair ARAC; independent members typically serve terms between 2–4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In appointing the Board, the Secretary of State will take account of diverse needs set out in the HER Act so Board members between them have experience across UKRI’s portfolio. Each Council consists of 5–12 independent members and an Executive Chair: Executive Chairs appointed by Secretary of State and independent members appointed by the Board on recommendation of the Executive Chair.
